##Part A — Creating Vectors and List
```{r}
## Question #1:
## Create a vector for the worker’s age.
ages <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24, 33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18)
ages
## How many data points?
length(ages)
## Find the minimum and the maximum value of worker’s age.
min(ages)
max(ages)
## Access the 13rd to 18th elements and 33th to 35th elements of worker’s Age.
ages[c(13:18, 33:35)]
## Access all but the 10th, 20th, 30th and 40th elements are not included.
ages[-c(10, 20, 30, 40)]
## Modify the 4th, 14th, 24th, and 44th elements with value = 0.
ages[c(4, 14, 24, 44)] <- 0
ages
```
```{r}
## Question #2:
# Get the summary statistical values of

data(rivers)
length(rivers)
sum(rivers)
mean(rivers)
median(rivers)
var(rivers)
sd(rivers)
min(rivers)
max(rivers)
# What is the result? Combine into a single vector.
results <- c(
  length = length(rivers),
  sum = sum(rivers),
  mean = mean(rivers),
  median = median(rivers),
  var = var(rivers),
  sd = sd(rivers),
  min = min(rivers),
  max = max(rivers)
)

results
```
```{r}
#Question #3:
# Create vectors according to the above table.
# 1. Power Ranking vector
power_ranking <- 1:25

# 2. Celebrity Name vector
celebrity_name <- c(
  "Tom Cruise", "Rolling Stones", "Oprah Winfrey", "U2", "Tiger Woods",
  "Steven Spielberg", "Howard Stern", "50 Cent", "Cast of the Sopranos",
  "Dan Brown", "Bruce Springsteen", "Donald Trump", "Muhammad Ali",
  "Paul McCartney", "George Lucas", "Elton John", "David Letterman",
  "Phil Mickelson", "J.K. Rowling", "Brad Pitt", "Peter Jackson",
  "Dr. Phil McGraw", "Jay Leno", "Celine Dion", "Kobe Bryant"
)

# 3. Pay vector (in millions)
pay <- c(
  67, 91, 225, 110, 90, 332, 302, 41, 52, 88, 55, 44, 55, 
  40, 235, 34, 40, 47, 75, 25, 39, 45, 32, 40, 31
)

# Combine into a data frame (optional but recommended)
forbes_ranking <- data.frame(PowerRanking = power_ranking, Celebrity = celebrity_name, Pay = pay)
forbes_ranking

# b. Modify the power ranking and pay of J.K. Rowling (Change power ranking to 15 and pay to 90).
power_ranking[19] <- 15
pay[19] <- 90


forbes_ranking

# Question #4:
# Initial List: Create a list of ten (10) vegetables
vegetables <- c("Carrot", "Broccoli", "Spinach", "Potato", "Tomato", 
                "Cucumber", "Cabbage", "Onion", "Garlic", "Eggplant")
vegetables
# Add 2 additional vegetables after the last vegetable in the list. What is the result?
# Appending 2 vegetables to the end of the vector
vegetables <- c(vegetables, "Zucchini", "Bell Pepper")
vegetables
# How many datapoints do you have?
length(vegetables)
# Add 4 additional vegetables after index 5. What is the result?
# Inserting 4 vegetables after index 5
new_veggies <- c("Cauliflower", "Lettuce", "Radish", "Pumpkin")

vegetables <- c(vegetables[1:5], new_veggies, vegetables[6:length(vegetables)])
vegetables
# d. How many datapoints does your vegetable list have?
length(vegetables)
```
